subject: Pathology
summary: Primary biliary cholangitis is an autoimmune attack on small intrahepatic bile ducts, leading to cholestasis, fibrosis and eventual cirrhosis. It mainly affects middle‑aged women and presents with pruritus before jaundice.

sections.p: PBC is a chronic, progressive cholestatic liver disease caused by lymphocyte‑mediated destruction of intrahepatic bile ducts. Diagnosis requires a combination of clinical features, laboratory evidence of cholestasis, and a positive anti‑mitochondrial antibody (AMA).

t.b: Is cholestasis present? High levels indicate bile duct injury.
Is an autoimmune process likely? Positive result confirms PBC.
Is the disease stage known? Histology shows portal inflammation and bile duct loss.

sections.p: Disease progression is staged by the Mayo Risk Score and histologic staging (Bismuth). Early stages show cholestasis; advanced stages reveal cirrhosis and portal hypertension.
b: Mayo Score: age, bilirubin, albumin, INR, alkaline phosphatase

t.b: Predicts 5‑year survival. Higher scores mean worse prognosis.
Assesses fibrosis extent; stage 4 indicates cirrhosis.

sections.p: The exact trigger is unknown, but genetic susceptibility and environmental factors (e.g., infections, toxins) initiate an autoimmune response against the pyruvate dehydrogenase complex.
b: Exposure to herbal remedies or chemicals

t.b: Is a genetic risk factor present? Certain alleles increase susceptibility.
Rule out infectious mimics of cholestasis.

sections.p: Patients first notice intense itching and fatigue. As disease advances, jaundice, dark urine, pale stools, and signs of portal hypertension appear.

whenToSeekHelp: Unexplained bleeding or severe abdominal pain

faq.q: What causes the itching in PBC?
faq.a: Accumulation of bile acids in the skin triggers pruritus.
